Top 10 AI highlights from the last 24 hours (Nov 9).

Anthropic shipped a new frontier model, Meta shipped its cheapest one, and OpenAI built a kill switch for its own research jobs.

1. Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. Same model, up to 30% faster than 5.1, and cheaper at $8 in / $40 out per million tokens. Fable is open to all users. Mythos stays gated to verified cyber and life-science orgs.

2. Fable 5.2 is now the top model on CursorBench at 60% on max effort, and 56.9% at default, up from 49.2% for 5.1. Anthropic still says start on Opus 5.5 and move up only for the hardest work.

3. Meta launched Muse Ember, its smallest model: $0.10 in / $0.50 out per million tokens, 1M context. Meta says it matches Haiku 5.5's best score at about a third of the cost. It's built to be the cheap worker under a bigger planner.

4. OpenAI detailed Control Room. Every research inference job registers an ID, and a stop decision halts model output within 35 seconds. If Control Room itself goes down, output stops too.

5. Nvidia released GR00T 2, an open world action model for robots. 71% average success across 50 tasks with one demo each, 95% with five. 100K hours of human video is open alongside it.

6. OpenAI dots can now connect to multiple local computers and pick which one runs a task. Build and test on one machine while you keep coding on another.

7. Automattic launched Spacefast: hosting, database, auth and domains for apps you build with ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor and other agents. A direct shot at Lovable-style builders.

8. Google put Maps Platform inside AI Studio. Prompt Gemini for a map app and get a live preview, no credit card needed to start.

9. Nuance Labs launched Emma, a face-to-face AI persona on a model that listens and talks at the same time, plus a beta API. They say its reply timing matches real speakers 89% of the time vs 35% for the next system.

10. ChatGPT Enterprise is now in AWS Marketplace, so companies can buy it against existing AWS commitments. Procurement just stopped being the blocker.

The pattern: big model plans, small model does the volume. Pick your stack by cost per task, not leaderboard rank.

Which of these are you actually switching to?
